title: The first day
summary: Your predecessor vanished and left clues instead of documentation. Move around the filesystem, list hidden files, peek into long files and find a buried key.

nodes.shortbread: Byte & Biscuit's oldest server, your new home

tasks.title: Count the chapters
tasks.text: Start by reading `~/WELCOME.txt` (`cat ~/WELCOME.txt`). Then: how many **chapter files** are in Gary's handbook, `/opt/biscuit/handbook`? Folders do not count.
hints: `cd /opt/biscuit/handbook` takes you there and `ls` lists what is inside. Or do both at once: `ls /opt/biscuit/handbook`.
`ls -l` puts a `d` at the start of every line that is a directory. Count only the lines that start with `-` (regular files).
Let the machine count for you: `ls /opt/biscuit/handbook/*.txt | wc -l`.

tasks.title: Gary's hidden Wi-Fi password
tasks.text: Gary "loved hiding things". Somewhere in his home directory `/home/gary` is the office Wi-Fi password. Find it and submit it (it looks like `DOJO{...}`).
hints: A plain `ls /home/gary` shows only two boring files. On Linux, a file whose name starts with a dot is **hidden** from `ls`.
`ls -a /home/gary` shows hidden files too (`-a` for all). Then `cat` the interesting one.

tasks.title: Meet the oven
tasks.text: `/var/log/oven.log` is over 5000 lines long, so `cat` would bury you in text. The **first line** names the oven. What is the oven called?
hints: `head file` shows the first 10 lines; `head -n 1 file` shows just one.

tasks.title: The last word
tasks.text: The **last line** of the same log reports the oven's final temperature before it shut down. What was it? (Just the number.)
hints: Want a few lines of context? `tail -n 5 /var/log/oven.log`. (On a real terminal, `less` lets you scroll, and `G` jumps to the end; the in-page terminal cannot run full-screen programs.)

tasks.title: The spare key
tasks.text: Gary swore the spare server-room key is a file named exactly `spare-key`, "somewhere under `/srv`". There are a lot of folders down there, and a couple of decoys. Submit the file's **full path**.
hints: Don't open folders one by one: `find` walks a whole tree for you. `find /srv` lists everything under `/srv`.
Narrow it down by name: `find /srv -name spare-key`. The name has to match exactly, so the decoys `spare-key.bak` and `spare-keyboard.txt` are skipped.

tasks.title: Make yourself at home
tasks.text: Unlike Gary, you keep notes. Create a folder `notes` in your home directory, and in it a file `day1.txt` that contains the word `biscuit` (plus anything else you like).

checks.fail_msg: There is no folder /root/notes yet (your home directory is /root, also written ~).
~/notes/day1.txt is missing or does not mention biscuit.

hints: `mkdir ~/notes` makes the folder. `~` is short for your home directory.
`echo 'Day 1: found the biscuit tin' > ~/notes/day1.txt` writes a line into a new file. `>>` instead of `>` appends another line.

steps.cmd: mkdir -p ~/notes && echo 'Day 1: survived. Found the biscuit tin.' > ~/notes/day1.txt
